pages.text: "Mom, I will watch rain here!" At the bow's very tip, Bung watched black clouds. Even tied to a post, the noodle boat rocked.
Bung wanted to see the first raindrop first. Ddori watched under the awning. Mom put out the stove and brought bowls inside.
Stronger wind! The awning flapped. A big rock almost toppled Bung. "Oh!" Both hands caught the boat edge.
Mom strode over and pulled Bung's arm inward. "All right. Let us stay here until the wind passes." Her calm voice settled Bung too.
She set a broth bowl on the floor and shook it gently. Broth spilled at the edge; the center stayed calm. "Boats are the same. Wind blows? To the middle!"
All three sat in the boat's middle under the awning. Mom gave Bung an awning rope. Ddori gripped it with a little hand too.
Raindrops pattered, awning flapping, boat rocking. Seated together with the rope, no fear! Bung drew Ddori's hand close, gripping together.
The wind eased, then the boat calmed. Sun peeked beyond the awning. "I was not even scared, Mom!"
Bung counted on fingers. "One, wind blows? To the middle! Two, rope tight in both hands! Three, when wind rests, hold Mom's hand to stand! Wind blows? To the middle!"
At evening, Mom sat both on her knees and patted their backs. "Wind passes. We wait in the middle." Cheek on her shoulder, Bung whispered, "Wind blows? To the middle!"
